quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to allow for movement.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet because it could become loose and cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This keeps you in control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: Which formation keeps a group of riders closest together?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps a group close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol consumption is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slowed body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down physical and mental functions.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handgrip.

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Always stay in the left part of the lane.
Always stay in the right part of the lane.
Use the best path, even if it doesn't follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the best path, even if it doesn't follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions can change. Be ready to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve may not follow the exact curve of the road.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually safe. Stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging to stop the weave will make things worse.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Don't ride down the center of a lane in wet conditions. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best, but it depends on traffic and other conditions.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Apply them firmly. Do not panic if the brakes lock up.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Distance is easier to judge at night than during the day.
High beam headlights always make it harder to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle properly while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Look through the turn to plan the best path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan the best path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from an entrance ramp may not see you. How can you help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane because it is not your responsibility to be seen.
Move to another lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can do so safely.
Weave back and forth in your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if it is safe to do so. If there is no other lane, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: What often causes a motorcycle to move into another lane while turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Taking the turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Entering a curve too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular with white background and black text or symbols. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which item is not protective riding gear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection even with a helmet.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while riding too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle will accelerate too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while riding too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: Always the right portion of the lane.
Always the center portion of the lane.
Always the left portion of the lane.
It changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position and no position to always avoid. Change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of being in a crash?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Communicate your intentions by using your turn signals and brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, signal your intentions, and keep space around you. Look for and avoid hazards. Be ready to react to anything.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle in a parallel parking space on the side of a road, how should it be parked?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 90-degree angle with the front wheel touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: In West Virginia, park motorcycles on the side of the road at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
You should allow a shorter following distance at night.
You should always maintain the same following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distance because there are fewer visual clues. Allow a longer following distance when riding at night than during the day.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about hazards and road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is an advantage of a brightly-colored helmet?

options.text: It may make it easier for other people to see you.
It doesn't help improve your visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may make it easier for other people to see you.
questions.explanation: A bright-colored helmet provides protection in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.
